hints: Focus on what is swapped in the organic molecule, the Br atom is replaced by an OH group from water.
Notice the starting halogenoalkane is primary, with the Br on a carbon attached to only one other carbon.
Connect the use of water as a reactant that splits to supply OH with the special name for this substitution, and recall which mechanism primary halogenoalkanes favour.
walkthrough:
**See what happens to the organic molecule**

Look closely, the C-Br bond becomes a C-OH bond. That is substitution of Br by OH, not removal to form a double bond.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{HBr}$$

**Name this type of substitution with water**

When a bond is broken by reaction with water, with H going one way and OH the other, we call it hydrolysis. Here water supplies the OH for the alcohol and H for HBr, so it fits perfectly.

**Check oxidation and mechanism to confirm**

Oxidation number of the carbon stays the same, so it is not redox. And because 1-bromopropane is primary, the carbocation would be unstable, so it favours $S_N2$ attack by water, not $S_N1$.

options.A: Elimination of a halogenoalkane removes HBr to form a C=C double bond, such as propene. Here no double bond forms, Br is replaced by OH to give propan-1-ol, so this is substitution, not elimination.
options.B: This is hydrolysis, which means cleavage by water. The $\text{C-Br}$ bond is broken and water provides $\text{OH}$ to make the alcohol and $\text{H}$ to make $\text{HBr}$. It is also a nucleophilic substitution reaction.
options.C: In redox the oxidation numbers must change. Carbon attached to Br in $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ and carbon attached to O in $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ have the same oxidation state, so no oxidation or reduction occurs.
options.D: $S_N1$ needs a stable carbocation intermediate and is favoured by tertiary halogenoalkanes. 1-bromopropane is primary, so it forms a very unstable primary carbocation and reacts mainly by the $S_N2$ mechanism instead.
